narrative.intro: Regents of the University of California has recorded $1.2B in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date. Regents received 3 awards this fiscal year, with an average award size of $391M. Obligations fell 10.3% year over year. Department of Energy is the dominant buyer, accounting for $1.2B of obligations. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences is the largest market for Regents, with $1.2B in obligations. Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools and Computer Facilities Management Services are secondary markets, at $4M and $31.3K respectively. Historical totals show large swings: FY23 was $982M, FY24 was $1.4B, and FY25 was $1.3B. Small early-year totals appear in FY21 and FY22 at $67.4M and $6.7M. The current-year totals are partial, covering fiscal year to date, and the largest buying agency and market both match the $1.2B total for FY2026 to date.

sections.heading: How did obligations change year over year?
sections.body: Obligations fell 10.3% year over year. FY25 obligations were $1.3B and FY26 obligations are $1.2B for the fiscal year to date. Earlier years show FY24 at $1.4B and FY23 at $982M, indicating large annual swings in obligations.

sections.heading: Where are the dollars concentrated?
sections.body: Department of Energy accounts for $1.2B of obligations for FY2026 to date. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences accounts for $1.2B of market obligations. Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools account for $4M and Computer Facilities Management Services accounts for $31.3K.

faq.q: How much does Regents of the University of California make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Regents of the University of California has $1.2B in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date. Regents received 3 awards this fiscal year, with an average award size of $391M. Current-year totals are partial and cover fiscal year to date.

faq.q: Which agencies buy from Regents of the University of California?
faq.a: Department of Energy buys from Regents of the University of California and accounts for $1.2B in obligations for FY2026 to date. Department of Commerce is a secondary buyer with $31.3K in obligations.

faq.q: What does Regents of the University of California sell to the government?
faq.a: Regents of the University of California sells research and development services in the physical, engineering, and life sciences to the government, totaling $1.2B in obligations for FY2026 to date. Regents also supplies services classified under Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools at $4M and Computer Facilities Management Services at $31.3K.

faq.q: Which Regents of the University of California contracts are expiring soon?
faq.a: Regents of the University of California has expiring-contract details not provided in these figures, but current FY2026 to date obligations total $1.2B. Review agency and procurement notices for specific contract expiration dates.
